title: The null base case
prompt: Why does almost every tree DFS start with `if (node == null) return ...;`?
options: Leaves have null children, so recursion inevitably reaches null — the base case defines what an empty subtree is worth
null nodes are common in the input arrays
explanation: dfs(leaf.left) is dfs(null). Defining the empty tree's value (0 for counts, true for validity checks, null for searches) is usually the whole trick.

title: Drill: tree sum
prompt: From memory: return the sum of all node values via DFS recursion. Base case: null contributes 0. Combine: node.val + left sum + right sum.
hints: Three lines: null check, then val + recurse left + recurse right.

title: Drill: count nodes (DFS)
prompt: From memory: return the total number of nodes via DFS. Base case: null is 0. Combine: 1 + left count + right count.
hints: Three lines: null check, then 1 + recurse left + recurse right.
